question.text: Will Safe Superintelligence (SSI) release an AI model to the public in 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as Yes if SSI releases an AI model to the public before 12:00 AM PT on January 1, 2027 according to [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions).
question.fine_print:
Any AI model which is officially a product of SSI (the company) will qualify.

"To the public" means that members of the general public are able to use the AI model for free or for a fee. A company announcement, a closed beta, or a public demo will not be sufficient on its own.

If for any reason SSI fails to release an AI model to the public as detailed above, including ceasing business operations before releasing its AI model, this question will resolve as No.

A public release qualifies notwithstanding that it may be restricted to certain countries or to users who have verified their identity in some way, provided that some members of the general public are able to access the model.

***
This question's information (resolution criteria, fine print, background info, etc) is synced with an [original identical question](https://www.metaculus.com/questions/46082) which opened on 2026-10-26 17:00:00. This question will resolve based on the resolution criteria and fine print of the linked original question. However, if this question would resolve differently than the original question, then this question will be annulled. Additionally, if the original question's resolution could have been known before this question opened, then this question will be annulled.

research:
I found no evidence that SSI has released a public model as of 2026-11-03. Everything SSI has said officially predates the rumors. Only about two months are left, and the Polymarket market on this question prices about 20% for a release by Dec 31.

### 1. Resolution source
- The question resolves on "credible sources," and the deciding signal is official SSI channels. SSI's homepage, fetched 2026-11-03, shows only the mission statement, hiring and links to Apply, Updates and Contact. There is no product, model, API or waitlist. [ssi.inc](https://ssi.inc/)
- The Updates page, fetched 2026-11-03, has three entries. The newest is 2026-07-26, the NVIDIA partnership, which says SSI's compute will scale tenfold. The others are 2025-07-03 (Daniel Gross left and Sutskever became CEO) and 2024-09-04 (a $1B raise). No model release is listed. [ssi.inc/updates](https://ssi.inc/updates)
- 2026-10-22: Wikipedia was last edited on this date. It lists no model releases, and its last 2026 event is the NVIDIA deal with a planned $5B investment. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Safe_Superintelligence_Inc.)

### 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question. Third-party trackers say that as of 2026-10-26 SSI had released no model, API, paper, waitlist or product. Another says the Updates page showed no launch as of 2026-10-09. [vorplabs](https://vorplabs.com/models/labs/safe-superintelligence), [getclerion](https://getclerion.com/resources/what-is-safe-superintelligence-ssi-and-is-it-the-same-6ad01f8ee7c635924cca9d5d)
- I found no news from late October or early November 2026 about an SSI model, launch date or beta. None of the news articles provided to me mentions SSI.

### 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-09 (exact date not visible): Polymarket posted on X that SSI was "projected to finally unveil its first public model next month. 53% chance." That presumably meant October, and it didn't happen. I couldn't open the post (HTTP 402). [X/Polymarket](https://x.com/Polymarket/status/2103202072522842430)
- 2026-09: A "confirmed vs rumoured" roundup found no release, paper or product as of 2026-08-24. [AIToolsReview](https://aitoolsreview.co.uk/insights/ilya-sutskever-superintelligence-model)
- 2026-08-25/26: BigGo reported that SSI's first model was "reportedly" debuting that week. The evidence was thin:
  - a16z partner Martin Casado tweeted "Just got access to a new model" without naming it (a16z is an SSI investor).
  - Andrew Curran passed on unverified talk of a "non-frontier lab" making a continual-learning breakthrough.

  No release followed. [BigGo](https://finance.biggo.com/news/7889e564-005b-4e69-bcff-74319f310ac2)
- 2026-08-26: Globes relayed investor Gavin Baker's claim, plus unnamed experts saying a model was in testing. Nothing appeared on SSI's channels. [getclerion](https://getclerion.com/resources/what-is-safe-superintelligence-ssi-and-is-it-the-same-6ad01f8ee7c635924cca9d5d)
- Early 2026-08: Gavin Baker said on the Invest Like the Best podcast that SSI would release its first model in August. This is the only source behind the rumor, and it was never confirmed. [cryptobriefing](https://cryptobriefing.com/ssi-superintelligence-model-august-release/), [orcarouter](https://www.orcarouter.ai/blog/ssi-first-model-release-date)
- 2026-07-27: SSI and NVIDIA announced a long-term partnership, including Vera Rubin systems and an NVIDIA investment reported at about $5B. [NVIDIA](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/ilya-sutskevers-safe-superintelligence-inc-and-nvidia-announce-long-term-strategic-partnership), [Calcalist](https://www.calcalistech.com/ctechnews/article/qy9eg5jw4)
- 2025-11: On the Dwarkesh podcast, Sutskever said superintelligence was 5 to 20 years away, SSI might deploy something earlier, and any release would be gradual. In 2024 SSI had said its "first product will be the safe superintelligence." [Dwarkesh](https://www.dwarkesh.com/p/ilya-sutskever-2)

### 4. Base rates
- SSI has released no public model in about 29 months since it was founded in June 2024, so it has never released one in any comparable two-month window.
- Rumored dates have already passed without a release: August 2026 (Baker), the "this week" report of late August, and an implied October 2026 (the Polymarket post).
- A release that does come may not count. Sutskever said any release would be gradual, and a closed or invite-only beta is explicitly excluded. That makes a qualifying public release harder than a debut announcement.
- Comparable "secretive" labs tend to reach the public through a waitlist or closed beta first. This is a general pattern, not a measured rate.

- The Kalshi markets provided are about other companies and aren't relevant.
- I found no Metaculus community figure or expert forecast that is public for the original question (46082).

### 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- I found no scheduled SSI event, conference talk or announced launch date between now and 2027-01-01.
- Things that could still matter:
  - an SSI post on ssi.inc/updates or X
  - Sutskever interviews or talks (NeurIPS in early December is a common venue)
  - reports of a new funding round or of NVIDIA Vera Rubin capacity coming online
  - new investor hints like Casado's or Baker's
- To watch: a closed beta or invite-only release would not count, but it could come before a public release in 2027.

- I could not find a reliable base rate for well-funded labs with no products launching within a given 2-month window.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) About 2 months remain, until 12:00 AM PT on January 1, 2027. For Yes, SSI must make an official SSI model usable by members of the general public, free or paid, before that deadline. An announcement, a closed beta, an invite-only release or a demo does not count.

(b) The status quo is No. SSI has released no model, API, waitlist or product in about 29 months, and its site and Updates page, checked 2026-11-03, show nothing product-related.

(c) Base rate: SSI has never released a model in any two-month window since its founding. Its stated strategy is a "straight-shot" with a gradual release. Secretive frontier labs usually start with a closed beta or waitlist, which would not count here. For a pre-product lab with no announced launch, the chance of a general-availability release within a given two-month window is roughly 5-10%.

(d) Evidence:
- **For Yes:**
  - The NVIDIA partnership on 2026-07-27 includes a tenfold compute scale-up and about $5B of investment.
  - Gavin Baker claimed in early August 2026 that a release was coming that month.
  - Martin Casado's late-August tweet "got access to a new model" and talk of a continual-learning breakthrough suggest some model may be in testing.
  - Polymarket's Dec 31 contract is at 20%.
- **For No:**
  - Every rumoured date has passed with nothing: August, the late-August "this week" report, and the implied October from Polymarket's September post.
  - Polymarket's Nov 30 contract is at 0.7%, so it sees almost no chance in November.
  - Polymarket's Dec 31 price has fallen from about 41% to 20%.
  - Sutskever has committed to a gradual release, which points toward a restricted beta first.
  - No launch event is scheduled.

(e) Scenarios:
- **No:** SSI keeps quiet through December, or at most announces a research result or a limited partner or tester program. A public release, if any, slips to 2027.
- **Yes:** With Vera Rubin capacity and investor pressure, SSI ships a public chat or API product in December, perhaps around NeurIPS, even if it is rate-limited or limited to some countries.

(f) I start from a base rate of about 7%. The market anchor is 20%, but its internal structure is odd: 0.7% by Nov 30 but 20% by Dec 31 implies about 19% for December alone, with no scheduled catalyst. That suggests a thin market or one anchored on earlier hype. The repeated failed rumours, and the exclusion of closed betas, argue for staying below the market. I settle around 10%, above the base rate because of the compute deal and signs that a model is in testing.

Probability: 10%

(a) About two months remain, until 12:00 AM PT on January 1, 2027. For Yes, SSI must make a model that is officially its own product usable by members of the general public, free or paid, as reported by credible sources. An announcement, a closed beta, an invite-only release or a demo does not count.

(b) The status quo outcome is No. SSI has released no product, API or waitlist in about 29 months. As of November 3, 2026, its homepage and Updates page show nothing new since the NVIDIA deal in July.

(c) The base rate is low:
- SSI has released nothing in any of the roughly 14 two-month windows since it was founded.
- A secretive lab that says "the first product will be superintelligence" rarely ships quickly.
- Even when such labs ship, a gradual or closed beta usually comes first, and that would not count here.

A reasonable base rate for a qualifying release in a given two-month window is about 3 to 5%. It is raised somewhat by the 2026 signals: the tenfold compute increase and the rumors.

(d) Evidence on each side:
- **For Yes:**
  - The NVIDIA partnership on July 27, 2026, with about $5B and a tenfold scale-up in compute.
  - Gavin Baker's claim in August 2026 of an August release.
  - Martin Casado's "new model" tweet and expert talk of a model in testing on August 25 and 26.
  - Polymarket's Dec 31 contract still at 20%.
- **For No:**
  - Three rumored dates (August, late August, October) have passed with nothing.
  - SSI's official channels have said nothing as of November 3.
  - Sutskever has committed to a "gradual release," which points to a closed beta first.
  - Polymarket prices a release by November 30 at only 0.7%, which implies almost nothing is expected soon.

(e) Scenarios:
- **No:** SSI keeps training on the new compute and perhaps gives investors or partners private access. Any debut is a limited preview, and public access slips into 2027.
- **Yes:** SSI announces a model at or around NeurIPS in December and opens a paid API or chat interface to the public, even if access is restricted by region or verification.

(f) Moving from the base rate to my estimate:
- I start at the market's 20% for Dec 31, which matches this question's wording closely.
- The structure of the market looks inconsistent: 0.7% for November but about 19% for December alone, with no known December catalyst. That looks like longshot bias or thin liquidity on the later contract. The same market also fell from about 41% as earlier rumors failed.
- The rule excluding closed betas further reduces the chance of a qualifying release.

I settle between the base rate of about 5% and the market's 20%, at around 10%.
